name: orb_retest_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: After an ORB breakout, the ORB_high or ORB_low level often gets retested 1-3 hours later as mid-day institutional flow revisits the morning's price discovery zone. When the retest holds (price touches ORB_high/low but doesn't close below/above it), it confirms the level as genuine support/resistance and provides a second entry opportunity with higher conviction than the original breakout. Retests are more reliable than initial breakouts because they represent the market's second assessment of the level, incorporating hours of additional price information. The inefficiency exists because most ORB traders take only the initial breakout and don't monitor for subsequent retests, which occur on ~60% of successful breakout days.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; initial ORB breakout occurred earlier in session
indicators: retest_up = low within 0.1% of ORB_high_15 AND close > ORB_high_15 (touched and bounced)
retest_down = high within 0.1% of ORB_low_15 AND close < ORB_low_15 (touched and rejected)

conditions: retest_up == True (price retested ORB_high and bounced)
close > ORB_high_15 at retest bar close (level held)
RSI_14 > 40 (not deeply oversold, bounce has energy)
long.confirmation: bounce bar at retest has lower wick touching ORB_high area AND close in upper half of bar

conditions: retest_down == True (price retested ORB_low and got rejected)
close < ORB_low_15 at retest bar close
short.confirmation: rejection bar at retest has upper wick touching ORB_low area AND close in lower half of bar

entry.entry_price: limit order at ORB_high_15 + 0.02% (long) or ORB_low_15 - 0.02% (short) — slight offset for confirmation

exit.target: session high at time of retest (for longs) + 0.5 * ORB_range_15 (new leg up expected after retest confirmation)
exit.stop_loss: 0.3 * ORB_range_15 below ORB_high (long) or above ORB_low (short)
exit.trailing_stop: after reaching prior session high (long), trail at ORB_high level
exit.signal_exit: if close breaks ORB level by > 0.15% against position (support/resistance broken), exit immediately

filters.time_filter: retests between 10:30-14:00 IST; retests after 14:00 may be end-of-day positioning, not genuine
filters.volume_filter: retest bar volume should be LOWER than breakout bar volume (healthy pullback, not new selling/buying wave)
filters.trend_filter: stock must still be above (long) or below (short) VWAP at retest time
filters.event_filter: skip if major intraday news released between breakout and retest
other_filters: retest must occur 1-3 hours after initial breakout; immediate retests (< 30 min) are usually failed breakouts, not healthy retests

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — retest trading requires monitoring and patience; most traders don't wait for the retest opportunity

weaknesses: Not all breakouts retest — ~40% of valid breakouts continue without retesting the ORB level, meaning this strategy misses a large portion of profitable ORB moves
Distinguishing a 'healthy retest' from a 'reversal through the level' in real-time is difficult; the 0.3 * ORB_range stop is tight and can be hit by normal volatility at the level
The 1-3 hour delay between breakout and retest means the strategy holds capital idle for extended periods, reducing capital efficiency
prior_art: Edwards & Magee (1948) on throwback/pullback to breakout levels; Brooks (2009) on retest entries. Bulkowski (2005) statistics on throwback frequency and reliability.
notes: Edge math: 0.64 * 38bps - 0.36 * 18bps = 24.32 - 6.48 = 17.84bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.84bps/trade. At 0.7 trades/day (retests don't always occur), daily ~6.2bps. The 26bps estimate is per retest signal day. Best combined with initial breakout strategy — take breakout trade first, add to position on retest.
